evidence.claim: This part of US 202 has carried three route numbers.
evidence.quote: Modern US 202 in Litchfield County was originally part of CT 25 (New Milford to Torrington) and CT 4 (Torrington to Canton.) The portion between Danbury and New Milford was then just US 7. In 1963, CT 4 was shifted southward with CT 25 extended along modern US 202 to Canton. In 1974, US 202 was moved to its modern alignment.

evidence.claim: Gillette’s Grist Mill retains the machinery that turned moving water into ground grain.
evidence.quote: Elements of the power generation and transmission equipment dating to c. 1870 survive, including the water wheel and a series of iron gears that connect it to drive shafts that rotated the grindstones.

evidence.claim: On the north bank of the Nepaug, west of the Maple Hollow Road crossing, the wooden building sits on a high stone foundation containing a wheel pit.
evidence.quote: It is set on the northern bank of the Nepaug River, a short way west of where Maple Hollow Road crosses.  Although the area supported more industry in the 19th century, this is the only surviving industrial building amid a cluster of houses.  It is a 2+1⁄2-story wood-frame structure set on a high stone foundation that include a large wheel pit.

evidence.claim: The surviving equipment appears to date to about 1870: a water wheel and iron gears connected to the grindstone drive shafts.
evidence.quote: Elements of the power generation and transmission equipment dating to c. 1870 survive, including the water wheel and a series of iron gears that connect it to drive shafts that rotated the grindstones.

evidence.claim: Joseph Gillette’s children acquired the mill in 1840, but it struggled as milling grew larger and more regional.
evidence.quote: The gristmill was acquired by his children in 1840, but did not thrive as grain milling operations became increasingly larger and regional

evidence.claim: It had shut down by 1880; portions of the water raceways survive.
